missions.title: missions

mission.list.effect: Read missions/task trees, acceptance evidence and reported usage coverage

mission.control.effect: Start approved branches, pause future launches, stop owned runs or redirect dormant task; completed evidence immutable
mission.control.pre: Known mission/task branch; start needs fingerprint-bound owner approval; redirect only dormant/blocked task and nonempty route/prompt patch

mission.create.effect: Persist draft mission and dormant waiting tasks; nothing launches
mission.create.pre: Nonblank goal/checks; 1–100 unique explicit task IDs; safe folders/routes; acyclic internal needs; positive recognized budgets; exact ID retries

draft-mission.goal: Read mission inventory, review explicit task graph and save dormant draft

supervise-mission.goal: Read actual branch state and choose pause or stop

verify-retained-status.goal: Verify that the selected mission has the expected ID and draft/running/paused/stopped state

mission-draft.constraints: Draft storage launches nothing. IDs unique, needs internal and acyclic; choose concrete completion evidence and positive token/time limits. Start requires owner approval fingerprint for exact mission/branches.
mission-draft.question: Do tasks, prerequisites, route and acceptance checks express the requested goal?

branch-control.constraints: Pause leaves running tasks active; stop cancels selected owned runs and dependent branches. Neither changes completed evidence. Confirm exact mission/task scope before decision.
branch-control.question: Pause future launches or stop owned runs?

pitfalls.recovery: Repair explicit needs graph; draft refused before storage

pitfalls.failure: Token budget waits for unknown usage
pitfalls.recovery: Wait for transport-reported usage; do not estimate model text

pitfalls.failure: Task done interpreted as accepted quality
pitfalls.recovery: Read evidence and explicit checks; evidence_ready_for_review still requires review
Pause/reconcile running work; completed evidence immutable, create fresh task intent

pitfalls.failure: A Claude Code or Codex task waits with 'Holding: ... limit at N%'
pitfalls.recovery: Its plan window passed Night Shift resources holdAtPlanPercent (default 70); it starts by itself after the shown reset. Raise or null holdAtPlanPercent only when Paul says so.

frontier: Mission semantic quality and cash cost are not generated by summary
Unreported transport token usage prevents exact budget admission

attention.list.effect: Read outstanding approvals, waiting/failed runs and blocked tasks with source IDs; no automatic repair

watch.create.effect: Arm event-driven one-shot notification; optional approved follow-up uses durable scheduler

watch.list.effect: Read watch conditions/outcomes and follow-up schedule/run identities
watch.list.pre: Workspace watch store readable; offset >=0, limit 1–100

triage-attention.goal: Read pending approvals, blocked tasks and recent failed runs before intervention

watch-run.goal: Inspect retained watches, review terminal/waiting conditions and arm a notification

verify-retained-status.goal: Verify the chosen one-shot watch identity and armed/fired/cancelled/blocked/uncertain status

verify-effect-watch-create.goal: Verify the actual effect through fresh owning observers

pitfalls.recovery: Inspect the receipt boundary and run the actual application journey for its remaining frontier

renderer.title: Renderer pane acknowledgement

pane.observe.pre: Authenticated owner renderer uses this workspace event channel

pane.show.effect: Request a pane; completion waits for mounted visible content acknowledgement
pane.show.pre: Authenticated owner renderer uses this workspace event channel

show-observed-pane.goal: Mount the requested pane and verify its fresh rendered content

pitfalls.failure: No renderer content report or stale observation
pitfalls.recovery: Mount in the owner shell and report content over /api/ui/ack; never invent a renderer receipt

frontier: Claude UI wiring and real Neyvia renderer mount/content proof remain required; queued pane events are incomplete
guidance: ACK observation: paneId, runtimeId, kind, target, contentHash (SHA-256 of UTF-8 displayed content), mounted, visible. Heartbeat at most 5 seconds; reports expire after 30 seconds. File content uses normalized editor text.

schedule.title: schedule

schedule.list.effect: Read durable follow-up records and outcomes; no new launches

schedule.after.effect: Translate relative delay once into durable follow-up; retries keep original timestamp

schedule.cancel.effect: Persist cancelled status; fired follow-ups require separate run reconciliation

schedule.create.effect: Persist one pending follow-up and wake workspace scheduler; empty scope means notification only
schedule.create.pre: Nonblank stable requestId; future timezone-qualified when; retry prompt/scope/time identical; chat scope read-only with safe folder and supported harness

remind-after.goal: Read follow-ups, review reminder and schedule one notification after specified seconds

cancel-pending.goal: Read schedule intent and cancel only selected pending follow-up

verify-retained-status.goal: Verify that the chosen follow-up has the expected ID and waiting/cancelled/done/blocked outcome

verify-effect-schedule-after.goal: Verify the actual effect through fresh owning observers

time.title: time

time.now.effect: Return precise UTC/local ISO timestamps and Unix seconds

time.budget.effect: Return advisory deadline risk and verification reserve; never stop agent work
time.budget.pre: Optional deadline has explicit timezone; estimates/reserve nonnegative

timer.lap.effect: Persist one checkpoint and interval measurement; exact retry replays saved lap
timer.lap.pre: Existing running timer with <1000 laps; stable lapId <=160 chars and label 1–200; repeated lapId must match intent

timer.list.effect: Read paged timer inventory with explicit nextOffset

timer.read.effect: Read elapsed measurement and paged laps; restarted-process values marked wall_clock_recovered_estimate

timer.start.effect: Persist running elapsed timer; same intent replays, stopped ID cannot restart a new measurement
timer.start.pre: ID nonblank <=160 chars; label 1–200 chars; positive finite targetSeconds; existing ID must match label/phase/target

timer.stop.effect: Persist stopped measurement; repeat stop replays it; never cancel associated work

start-timer.goal: Start a distinct elapsed-work measurement and verify running state

lap-and-stop.goal: Read elapsed timer, decide checkpoint, then record one lap and stop

checkpoint.constraints: Timer is elapsed time, not CPU/provider cost. Stop only measurement; it does not cancel work. A stopped ID cannot be reused for a new timing intent.
checkpoint.question: Record this completed checkpoint and stop measurement?

pitfalls.failure: Timer ID/lapId reused with different intent
pitfalls.recovery: Use new ID for new measurement; exact retries replay retained values
Report clockBasis=wall_clock_recovered_estimate and clockAnomaly; do not call it monotonic precision
Continue required work or report real blocker; timer does not stop it

pitfalls.failure: A lap is attempted on stopped timer or beyond 1000 laps
pitfalls.recovery: Start a distinct timer for next measurement; retain old evidence

frontier: No provider cost or CPU-time accounting in elapsed timers
Wall clock across restarts may change; do not use as calibrated performance benchmark
